text: In nineteen ninety-six, Europe's brand-new rocket blew itself up thirty-seven seconds after liftoff. Because one number was too big. Its guidance code was reused from the older Ariane four. One value, sideways speed, was squeezed from a sixty-four bit number into a sixteen bit one. Ariane five was faster. The number didn't fit. The computer crashed, and the backup, running the same code, crashed the same way. The nozzles swung hard over, the rocket started breaking up, and it destroyed itself. Four science satellites went with it. Dave said the old code worked fine.
